description: The National Waterway Network is a geographic database of navigable waterways and channels in and around the United States, made for analytical studies of navigation performance, for compiling commodity flow statistics and for mapping. It has a link layer and a node layer: links are line strings that follow actual shipping lanes (channels, Intracoastal Waterways, sea lanes, rivers) or represent paths in open water, with river name, river miles, length, waterway type and functional class; nodes mark river confluences, ports and facilities, intermodal terminals and USACE nodes, with about 224 USACE ports geocoded. It was created on behalf of the Bureau of Transportation Statistics, USACE, the Census Bureau and the Coast Guard by Vanderbilt University and Oak Ridge National Laboratory, and is published by the USACE Institute for Water Resources. Coverage is national, inland and coastal; on 26 September 2026 the feature service held 6,859 links and 6,255 nodes, last modified October 2025. Access is free as an ArcGIS feature service with query and extract, open without login. Caveats: open-water links are representative paths, not charted lanes, and attributes such as depth are not part of the network. The NWN is the routing graph for network flow, capacity planning, cascading failure and resilience studies of inland and coastal shipping, and complements the Inland Electronic Navigational Charts and the OpenTNSim model catalogued here.
